picks.title: Sitting Like a Buddha
picks.summary: Where are you located in your body? Most of us, without ever having chosen it, sense ourselves somewhere behind the eyes. Zazen instructions typically bundle two separable practices: disidentifying from thinking, and relocating the self in the belly. Contemporary mindfulness often teaches the first and omits the second. Zen's own instruction is to sit as a buddha rather than in order to become one, trusting a monastic container to do that work silently; outside such a container, this talk suggests, it has to be made explicit. picks.reason: Detailed Zen instruction on sitting practice and self-location in meditation.

picks.title: Buddhist Stories to Help You Let Go and Fall Asleep - Zen Buddhism for Rest

picks.title: The Open Gate
picks.summary:
In this Wednesday Night Dharma Talk, Sensei Fushin turns to the first two folds of the Eightfold Path—right view and right intention—the wisdom from which the rest of the path grows. Right view, he suggests, is not a belief we acquire but seeing what is actually here, before we add our story about it. “The eye opens. The heart leans,” he says — one sees, one moves, and they are not two.

picks.reason: Dharma talk on right view and intention as foundational Buddhist wisdom.
